label: Lancashire
note: Only Beacon Fell Traditional Lancashire is PDO (milk from north of the River Ribble). Crumbly Lancashire (1950s, high-acid, single day's milk) is made outside Lancashire too.

about.text: Lancashire is an English cow cheese from the county of Lancashire, traditionally made by mixing curds of two or three days.

steps.name: blend
steps.note: Curd of 2–3 days of different ages is blended; crumbly uses one day only.
Creamy 4–12 weeks, tasty 12 weeks to 24 months, crumbly 6–8 weeks.

processing.text: Creamy ripens 4-12 weeks, tasty 12 weeks to 24 months, crumbly 6-8 weeks.
